transcript: Let's go see an opera courtesy of Zohran Mamdani. If you didn't see, Mamdani announced a new initiative in partnership with the Metropolitan Opera where they are going to be giving away 70,000 free tickets. They're being given out via digital lottery. And somehow I won first try? So either it's pretty easy to win or I got very lucky. Either way, I was thrilled because I have been dying to see this production of LA Boheme at the met. This is one of those legendary productions that they just keep bringing back because it's so popular. Not only is it one of the most popular operas ever written, but this production specifically is kind of seen as like the Pinnacle. And as far as maximalist theatre goes, it does not get more lavish than this. At one point, there's, I think 250 people on stage, including a full marching band, a donkey and a horse. The sets are huge and intricate to the point where there were gaps every time the curtain opened. if you are someone that doesn't like the current trend of minimalism on Broadway, go see La Boheme at the met. this has everything that you are missing. And of course, it's the Met Opera, so it's some of the best opera singers in the world, a full 70* piece orchestra performing some of the most gorgeous music you'll ever hear. This is actually my second opera at the Metropolitan Opera, and it really Is something that I think everyone should experience at least once. Not only is the interior of the building and the theatre itself absolutely stunning, but there are very few places in the United States that are still doing opera at this scale and at this level. So even if you don't necessarily think that opera is for you, what better place to try it out than the best of the best? And that's why I love this new ticket initiative, where so many people are going to get to experience opera for the first time, completely for free. And I think it's going to create a lot of new opera fans who may not have been able to give opera a chance otherwise.
